properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (second pass, same day): after the shear fix above, a user-flagged visual check still showed this block overlapping paved streets. Root cause found: several blocks (PKN, PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, E4) had their OWN corner pixel positions misread during transcription -- e.g. PKN's west edge was recorded as pixel x=163 when the diagram's own gridline labels put it at x=355 (which is where the Illinois St anchor point itself was measured). This was a transcription slip, not a transform error -- the 6-point transform's anchors were unaffected (confirmed: A, B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3, F/G, H1, H2 were read correctly the first time). Re-read all 5 affected blocks' corners directly against their crop images' own labeled gridlines and recomputed. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (third pass): user-flagged overlap between HDY3/HDY1-2 and between E2/H1 and E3/H2 -- both were transcription errors (HDY1/2's diagonal notch was oversimplified into a plain rectangle that re-overlapped HDY3; E2/E3's bottom edge was misread as the row further south, landing on top of H1/H2). Re-read against the diagram's own gridlines and confirmed zero geometric overlap with the adjacent block this time. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 border-alignment audit): this block's north edge (its shared internal division with PKS, not a real street) was a plain diagram-corner-misread -- two independent grid-overlay crops of Figure 6.4.2 confirmed the true PKS/HDY3 divider sits at pixel y~927-932, ~55-60px north of where this file had it (y~985-992), which had left a real gap unclaimed by either polygon. Moved this block's NW/NE corners to pixel (374,927)/(591,927) -- matching PKS's own corrected south edge exactly -- via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Also shifted the next vertex (originally a small step just south of the old NE, presumably marking where this block's east edge begins its diagonal cut toward the southern point) north by the same amount, to preserve its position relative to the corrected NE rather than leaving it stranded mid-shape. The block's own southern extent (the far-south point corner) is unchanged, unaffected by this fix. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (second pass, same day): user-flagged visual check found the same-day fix above left a visible kink -- the un-shifted southern vertex no longer lined up with the block's true diagonal edge. Re-measured this block's ENTIRE shape programmatically instead of patching individual vertices: isolated this legend color (RGB [169,143,173]) in a fresh crop, connected-component labeled it, and extracted its precise contour (OpenCV, simplified to its 4 real corners). Result: NW(420,932), NE(591,932), a corner where the east edge turns into the diagonal cut (591,1027), and the block's own southern point (437,1195) in pixel space -- converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. This replaces both today's earlier patches with one clean, from-scratch re-measurement; confirmed zero overlap with PKS (north) and HDY1/2 (south, across the Irish Hill Playground gap). CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (streets/block-alignment review, prompted by a user request to audit street alignment sitewide): the pixel measurement above (NW/NE at y=932, from a 'fresh crop') turns out to have been taken from the same 2376x1836-resolution copy of Figure 6.4.2 that caused the confirmed resolution-mismatch bug on PKN and PKS's old traces (420*1.08=453.6... more precisely, this block's own values are exactly 1.08x this site's correct 2200x1700-resolution measurement: 932/1.08=863.0, 420/1.08=388.9, 591/1.08=547.2 -- all matching a fresh, independent re-measurement on page171.png to within 1px). Re-measured directly on page171.png: this block's true contour is (547,863)-(389,863)-(389,1107)-(404,1107)-(547,951) in pixel space (a slightly larger polygon than the old one, extending further south since the old trace's southern point (437,1195) was itself part of the same bad crop). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Confirmed touching (0m gap, 0 overlap) with the newly-corrected PKS to the north; the ~44m gap to HDY1/2 (part of Irish Hill Playground) is preserved as before. RE-INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (yet again, same day, after user feedback called the prior revert-and-redo cycle 'mostly a downgrade' and asked for a clarifying question rather than another guess): went back to first principles instead of more pixel geometry. Two checks, both requested by the user: (1) searched the D4D's own text (Section 4.11, Specific Streets Design Intent) for any description of 21st St being relocated or realigned -- found none; it describes 21st St as 'primarily serves as an alley from Illinois Street to the waterfront,' with no mention of a moved alignment. (2) Pulled real satellite imagery (src/satellite_check.py) directly over where DataSF's official centerline (CNN 15232000/15233000) says 21st St runs between Illinois and Michigan St -- it shows vegetation, graded dirt, a tree, and a vehicle-storage yard: zero pavement. So the earlier 'the D4D relocates 21st St' theory (this file's own prior REVERTED/RETRACTED entries) was an overreach from a real but simpler fact: DataSF's centerline here is a paper (platted, unbuilt) alignment, the same failure mode as three other already-excluded CNNs in street_geometry.py (12915000, 15200000, 15228000) -- not a deliberate relocation. Added CNN 15232000/15233000 to that same exclusion list, with the satellite evidence documented there. User's explicit instruction: note that this stretch of 21st St isn't built yet, but for this map's purpose (showing the planned FUTURE parcel state) treat the diagram's own drawn '21ST ST (NEW)' position as authoritative. Restored this block to its pure diagram-transform position accordingly -- the same value already found and confirmed multiple times this project (most recently before the mistaken ground-truth shift below). Area restored to ~2,699 sq m. REPOSITIONED 2026-09-17 (user override: 'take my input as override... turn that Michigan span into 21st st and adjust parcel positioning accordingly'): re-anchored to the corrected planned 21st St line (see pier70_21st_street.geojson -- built from Michigan St's own real terminus point, perpendicular to Illinois/Louisiana's real ~175.5-degree bearing), replacing the Figure 6.4.2 pixel-traced position used previously. Also user-instructed to ensure this block borders 22nd Street directly (the D4D diagram itself only brings this block's diagonal cut close to HDY1/2's own NW corner, leaving a small Irish Hill Corner Plaza sliver between it and 22nd St -- overridden per explicit instruction). North edge (NE/NW) shifted by the same amount as the adjacent PKS corners, preserving the touching relationship. Reshaped the block's whole south/diagonal portion: extended a new west edge straight down along Illinois St's own longitude from the (shifted) NW corner to the real 22nd St curb line (6.8m north of centerline), then connected east along that same curb to the repositioned HDY1/2's own NW corner (which was, in the same pass, also extended to the real 22nd St curb -- see that file), then up along HDY1/2's own diagonal edge back to its NW corner, replacing this block's old, shorter diagonal cut entirely. This new southern extension initially overlapped the real Illinois St street buffer by 31% (a real, substantial encroachment, not a normal corner sliver) -- clipped via shapely difference() against the real-street buffer, dropping the extension's own width along Illinois St to whatever real room exists there. Final area ~2,306 sq m (the north portion carried over from the PKS-anchored shift, plus this new Illinois-frontage extension down to 22nd St). Confirmed 0 overlap with the repositioned HDY1/2 (0m gap, touching) and re-clipped Irish Hill Playground against this new shape (see that file). RECONSIDERED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: this block and HDY1/2 should keep the diagonal disconnect via Irish Hill Playground, not touch directly): tried a version with a ~12m-wide gap preserved between this block's own Illinois-St extension and HDY1/2's west edge, for Irish Hill Playground to occupy down to 22nd St. Measured the REAL available space there directly: the real street buffer (Illinois St, CNN 7169001) extends east to within 2-9m of HDY1/2's own west edge along this whole stretch (checked at 4 latitudes between 22nd St and this block's own north portion) -- there isn't real room for a separate gap-preserving corridor without either cutting into Illinois St's own right-of-way or making HDY1/2 narrower. Reverted to touching HDY1/2 directly (0m gap) at the 22nd St corner, using the 9.8m curb+sidewalk offset -- this satisfies 'borders 22nd Street' but does NOT restore the diagonal disconnect; flagged this specific tension back to the user rather than silently picking a side. REDESIGNED 2026-09-17 (two user-flagged issues, same pass): (1) 'HDY3 and PKS should have the same width' -- this block's own north edge was still only ~39m wide (its old, pre-Michigan-extension measurement) while PKS grew to ~75m wide after its own Michigan St extension. Set this block's NE corner to PKS's exact SE corner (-122.386554, 37.75906638453553), matching PKS's width exactly and closing that gap to 0m. (2) 'resolve the HDY3/HDY1-2 diagonal disconnect' -- restored a real, meaningful gap to HDY1/2 (narrowed slightly in the same pass, see that file) for Irish Hill Playground to occupy, rather than touching directly as the prior round left it. Reshaped this block's southern portion as a clean quadrilateral: NW straight down Illinois St to 22nd St curb, then east along the curb to a point 6.7m short of HDY1/2's own (narrowed) west corner, then up to a point offset from HDY1/2's own NW corner by a similar margin, closing the gap on both sides. EXEMPTED FROM STREET CLIPPING: the naive version of this new southern portion was clipped 24-31% by the real street buffer near the Illinois/22nd corner and fell ~15m short of the real 22nd St curb -- checked via satellite and found this specific corner is Illinois St's own real diagonal on-street parking apron plus a private, currently-industrial paved yard (equipment/vehicle storage), not a public thoroughfare this block would need to cross -- the same 'plan the redevelopment, not today's ad hoc site use' reasoning already applied to HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground's own Michigan St exemptions. Exempted so this block reaches 22nd Street directly, per explicit instruction, rather than being cut down by a routine clip against a same-site informal condition. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (two more user-flagged issues, same review pass: 'HDY3 should border Illinois like PKS and PKN, in the continuity' and 'the diagonal you create between HDY3 and HDY1/2 should be made of 2 parallel edges'): (1) west-edge continuity -- this block's NW corner (v1) had never been put on the same real-Illinois-St-offset line as PKN's and PKS's own west edges (each was independently diagram/satellite-traced), leaving a several-meter 'wobble' where the three blocks' own west edges met. Recomputed all of PKN's SW corner, PKS's NW/SW corners, and this block's NW corner (v1) from one shared formula: interpolate real Illinois St's centerline (CNN 7169000) latitude at each corner's own latitude -- i.e. solve for the centerline's longitude there -- then offset 9.8m east (this project's standard curb+sidewalk allowance). This puts all three blocks' west corners exactly on one consistent line for the first time. v2 (this block's own southern extension of that same edge, down to the 22nd St corner) was shifted east by the identical delta as v1 (preserving the v1-v2 edge's own prior shape/bearing exactly) rather than independently re-solving v2 against both the Illinois and 22nd St offset lines -- that dual-offset intersection was tried first and produced a self-intersecting polygon (v2 landed east of v3, crossing the v3-v4 edge), because v3 is a fixed, judgment-call point in the same messy, exempted, real-world industrial corner (see EXEMPTED note above) and isn't itself pinned to a pure Illinois-line intersection. The applied fix keeps the polygon valid while still moving the whole west frontage onto the corrected line. (2) parallel corridor -- the gap this block leaves for Irish Hill Playground to reach HDY1/2 (v3-v4 edge) was not parallel to HDY1/2's own corresponding edge (v3-v0 in that file): bearings were 19.1 degrees vs 11.2 degrees, an 8-degree mismatch, visibly not a clean corridor on the map. Fixed by keeping v3 fixed (the 22nd St curb attachment) and this edge's own prior length (86.1m) unchanged, but rotating it to HDY1/2's own v3-v0 bearing (11.2 degrees, since that block's corners are more directly tied to established real-street offsets) -- confirmed the perpendicular gap between the two lines is now uniform (~17.0m) at both ends, i.e. genuinely parallel, versus varying before. Re-validated: polygon is simple/non-self-intersecting, 0 overlap with PKS and HDY1/2 (touching PKS with 0m gap as before). REBUILT 2026-09-17 (user-flagged, third time: 'HYD3 is too messed up' -- sent an unlabeled version of the map and asked to draw a replacement by hand): the formula-driven approach above, while internally consistent, produced a shape the user judged wrong on sight. User hand-drew both HDY3 and HDY1/2 directly on the unlabeled satellite map (out/pier70_unlabeled.png) and asked for their sketch to be used as the baseline, cleaned up for parallelism. Digitized their drawing: (1) matched the user's uploaded photo (a resized/JPEG-compressed crop) back to the exact source render via ORB feature matching against the unmodified basemap content (393/419 inlier keypoints, near-pure similarity transform -- scale 2.069x, negligible rotation/shear), confirming precisely where their crop sits in the full render's pixel space; (2) independently calibrated that full render's own pixel<->lon/lat mapping by re-rendering it with small marker dots at known vertices (this project's own already-committed HDY3/HDY1-2 corners) and detecting their pixel centers -- sub-pixel (<0.6px) residuals confirmed the fit; (3) isolated the user's hand-drawn lines by color (a bright saturated blue distinct from this map's own semi-transparent parcel fills) and extracted each shape's corners. Cross-checked the pipeline by transforming the user's drawn NE corner (which should coincide with the real, already-fixed HDY3/PKS shared corner) and found it landed within ~7m of that known point -- confirming the geo-registration itself, with the residual being ordinary hand-drawing imprecision. Final shape: NE corner kept exactly at the existing HDY3/PKS shared point (unchanged); NW corner snapped exactly onto PKS's own SW corner (the user's drawn point independently landed within ~2m of it, confirming their sketch already preserves the Illinois St continuity fixed earlier the same day) rather than the previous 22nd-St/Illinois-intersection formula; SW (22nd St) corner taken directly from the user's drawn point; corridor edge (facing HDY1/2) rotated to exactly match HDY1/2's own corresponding edge bearing (see that file) while preserving the user's own drawn edge length, keeping the corridor genuinely parallel (uniform ~17m gap) as requested. Re-clipped Irish Hill Playground against this new shape (322 sq m new overlap, since this shape reaches further into that space than the previous round's -- see that file). 0 overlap with PKS (unchanged shared edge) and HDY1/2 (17m corridor gap, confirmed parallel).
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. SNAPPED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's north edge had drifted 1.26m south of PKS's own south edge (both blocks were independently re-measured at different times and no longer shared an exact boundary, despite the diagram showing them as one continuous fill with only an internal divider line). Snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's south-edge coordinates exactly, closing the gap to 0m. RE-SNAPPED 2026-09-17 (same day): PKS itself was found to be badly mispositioned (60% of its area was being silently clipped away against the real 21st St -- see pier70_pks.geojson) and was shifted ~25m south to ground-truth against the real street. Re-snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's new south edge to stay attached; area dropped from ~2,699 to ~1,508 sq m as a direct, expected consequence of PKS moving into what was previously this block's own north portion. This block's own south/diagonal portion (touching HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground) is unchanged. INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'HYD3 too small relative to its peers based on drawing'): checked whether this shrinkage is a real bug (i.e., whether the same northward transform bias found on PKS/C1/PKN/Building 113-116 also affects this block's own south/diagonal portion, which would justify shifting HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground south too, restoring this block's diagram-implied size while keeping everything attached). Tested this directly: interpolated the real, official 22nd St centerline's latitude at HDY1/2's own south-edge longitudes (the nearest independently-checkable real street to this cluster) and compared to HDY1/2's current south edge -- found a clean ~14m gap with NO overlap, unlike PKS's 60% real-street overlap that justified its own correction. This is the opposite signature from a 'drawn too far north' bug: if the same bias reached this far south, HDY1/2 would itself be overlapping 22nd St, not comfortably clear of it. Conclusion: the 21st-St-row bias is local to that row and does not extend to this block's own south portion or to HDY1/2/Irish Hill Playground -- there is no evidence basis to shift them south to recover this block's pre-fix size. This block's current, smaller size is treated as the accurate, forced consequence of ground-truthing PKS (which shares this block's own north edge), not an unresolved bug. Flagging this conclusion explicitly per this project's no-fabrication rule: if a future source shows this block's own south/diagonal corners were independently misread (a diagram-reading error, not a bias-correction consequence), that would still warrant revisiting this specific block on its own.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Residential per Brookfield's leasing brochure (not 'parking support' as sometimes described secondhand), 65 ft max per Figure 6.4.2 (a uniform height, not a 40-65 ft range). Named for the former PG&E 'Hoedown Yard' that once occupied this area. Shown as a separate parcel from HDY1/2 in the D4D's own figure. No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.
